podcast.title: Created by Dave Rave Ogilvie (Skinny Puppy)
podcast.body: The group was formed by Dave Rave Ogilvie, known for his work with Skinny Puppy and other prominent artists like Nine Inch Nails, Marilyn Manson, and David Bowie. "created by Dave Rae Oglevy of Skinny Puppy. He also worked with Nine-H nails, Marilyn Manson, David Bowie and a bunch of others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Current Status as Defunct
podcast.body: The band appears to be defunct in recent times. "The band seems to be defunct these days."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dave Rave Ogilvie's Continued Production Work
podcast.body: Following Jackalope, Dave Rave Ogilvie has continued his career in music production and engineering. "Dave Rave Oglevy continues his production and engineering work."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Katie B as Voice and Face
podcast.body: Katie B, originally a receptionist at Brian Adams' Warehouse Studio in Vancouver, became the primary vocalist and public persona for Jackalope after meeting Dave Rave Ogilvie. "Things began to come together when he met Katie B, the receptionist at the warehouse studio, Brian Adams recording studio in Vancouver. They got along great, and she became the voice and the face of Jackalope."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Katie B's Post-Jackalope Projects
podcast.body: Katie B collaborated with Sébastien Lefebvre of Simple Plan on a Christmas EP and also formed a band called Nice Horse, which released a couple of country-tinged albums. "Meanwhile, Katie B went on to work with Sebastian LaFave of Simple Plan on a Christmas EP, plus she had a band called Nice Horse, which released a couple of albums. Those ones had more of a country vibe."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Notable Contributors to Music
podcast.body: Over the years, Jackalope's music featured contributions from a range of distinguished artists, including members of Sloan and Monster Magnet, Trent Reznor of Nine Inch Nails (who also co-produced), Alex Lifeson of Rush, and the three members named Don from Sons of Freedom. "Over the next few years, a number of really interesting artists contributed to Jackalope's music. The members of Sloan, the members of Monster Magnet, Trent Resner of Nine-H nails acted as a co-producer for a while. Alex Lifeson of Rush, and like I said, the three Don's from Sons of Freedom."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Theme Song for Degrassi: The Next Generation
podcast.body: Jackalope composed and performed the theme song for the television series "Degrassi: The Next Generation" from season 4 onwards. "If you were a fan of Degrassi, the next generation, Jackalope did the theme song from season 4 onward."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Toronto-Based Indie/Industrial/Electronic Group
podcast.body: Jackalope was an indie, industrial, and electronic music group based in Toronto. "They were an indie slash industrial slash electronic group from Toronto."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
